1	# A web page on the remote port (issue #230)
2	
3	The host serves a small page from the remote port it already has. Any
4	browser on the local network opens it, pairs from a URL in the pairing
5	window's QR code, lists the sessions with the waiting ones first, shows
6	a session's last response or screen, and sends a reply. The API is the
7	one the headset uses, plus one small read. The page is three files
8	under `web/`, embedded with `include_str!`. There is no build step and
9	no dependency.
10	
11	Line numbers are as of 7fe8949 in this worktree. "Facts" means
12	`facts/1/repo/facts.md`, cited by section and line.
13	
14	## Where this departs from the issue
15	
16	- **The pairing data goes in the fragment, not the query.** The URL is
17	  `https://<ip>:<port>/#code=…&key=…&id=…`.
18	  - A fragment never appears in the request line or in `Referer` (Facts,
19	    Settled, line 17). The code therefore never reaches the host's
20	    `RemoteRequest.query`, a proxy, or a log. A `?code=` would reach all
21	    three before any page script runs.
22	  - The page still calls `history.replaceState` first. Whether Safari,
23	    iCloud or the camera keep the original URL is unresolved (Facts,
24	    Unresolved, line 35), so the plan does not depend on it. The code's
25	    protection is what it already is: single use, five minutes, and
26	    three failures close the window.
27	- **Pairing waits for one tap, with a name field.**
28	  - The page shows "Pair as [name]" with a default taken from the user
29	    agent, and posts `/pair` only when the owner taps Pair.
30	  - The tap is needed because iPadOS Safari may identify itself as a Mac
31	    (Facts, Unresolved, line 36), and the dialog has no way to rename a
32	    device. So the name has to be chosen on the page.
33	- **The events socket is an enhancement. Polling is the default.**
34	  - Whether `wss://` connects in Safari after a certificate click-through
35	    is unresolved (Facts, Unresolved, lines 28–33).
36	  - The page first works by polling: `waiting` every 5 s, the open
37	    session's read every 5 s, and the lists every 30 s, only while the
38	    tab is visible.
39	  - When the socket opens, the page follows §4.4 and stops polling. When
40	    the socket fails, the header says "Live updates unavailable".
41	  - Under either answer, "a waiting session moves to the top without a
42	    reload" holds.
43	- **The page needs one new read: `GET /api/v1/device`.** It answers
44	  `{device_id, name, scope}`.
45	  - Only the `/pair` reply tells a device its scope (Facts, Settled,
46	    line 7), and the reply box depends on scope.
47	  - The page's first authenticated call on load is this read, so a 200
48	    or 401 here also decides between "paired" and "pair again".
49	- **Not every session gets a one-line excerpt.**
50	  - `SessionView` has no excerpt field (`control/src/lib.rs:637`). The
51	    Mac builds its excerpt from the transcript in
52	    `src/ui/cards.rs:558`, and the headset reads `last-response` once
53	    per session (`client/Sources/SwitchboardUI/BrowserView.swift:152-155`).
54	  - The cost of that on real data is unresolved (Facts, Unresolved,
55	    line 40). So the page reads `last-response` only for waiting Claude
56	    Code sessions, at most 8 of them, and for the session that is open.
57	  - Every other row shows its `waiting_reason`, or its `card` word.
58	  - An excerpt field on `SessionView` is a follow-up.
59	- **The certificate is reissued over the same key.** The issue does not
60	  mention this.
61	  - Today's certificate has no SAN, no EKU, and a `not_after` in the year
62	    4096 (`src/adapters/remote.rs:95-110`; Facts, Settled, line 10).
63	    Apple says connections with such a certificate "will fail" (Facts,
64	    Settled, line 11). Whether Safari or Chrome still offer a
65	    click-through for it is unresolved (Facts, Unresolved, line 27).
66	  - The plan builds a compliant certificate:
67	    - a SAN for the LAN IP, `127.0.0.1` and `localhost`;
68	    - the serverAuth EKU;
69	    - a validity of 800 days, reissued when fewer than 30 days remain or
70	      when the current address is missing from the SAN.
71	  - The SPKI does not change, so every native pin stays valid (spec §5:
72	    "a certificate reissued from the same key … still verifies").
73	- **A browser's acceptance of the certificate is not permanent.**
74	  - Chrome forgets a bypass after 7 days (Facts, Settled, line 18), so on
75	    Chrome the warning comes back once a week.
76	  - How long Safari remembers one is unresolved (Facts, Unresolved,
77	    line 34). The page assumes nothing about it.
78	- **"Identity changed" appears after the browser's own warning.**
79	  - After a key rotation, the browser shows its interstitial before any
80	    page script runs (Facts, Settled, lines 18–19).
81	  - Once the owner accepts, the page compares `/info`'s key with the one
82	    it stored at pairing and shows "identity changed, pair again".
83	- **The page learns "revoked" over REST, never from the socket.**
84	  - A refused upgrade reaches the page only as a 1006 close (Facts,
85	    Settled, line 15). The page therefore follows every socket close
86	    with a `GET device` call. A 401 there shows "No longer paired".
87	  - The host gives a revoked device and a rotated pairing the same 401
88	    (`src/app.rs:3127-3157`). The page tells them apart from the key it
89	    stored, not from the reply.
90	- **`SameSite=Strict` does not isolate one port from another.**
91	  - Every port on one IP is same-site, and a cookie is sent to all of
92	    them (Facts, Settled, line 16).
93	  - To keep two instances from colliding, the cookie is named after the
94	    `server_id`.
95	  - To stop another page on the same IP from riding on the cookie, a
96	    cookie is accepted only on a request carrying `X-Switchboard-Page: 1`
97	    (a cross-origin page cannot send that header without a preflight the
98	    host never answers), or on an upgrade whose `Origin` is the host's
99	    own (Facts, Settled, line 13: browsers must send `Origin`).
100	  - The plan accepts that the cookie also reaches any other HTTPS service
101	    on the owner's own Mac's IP. That cost buys a token that no script
102	    can read.
103	- **The QR's address has to be reachable.**
104	  - The QR prints `local_address()` even while the port is bound to
105	    loopback, and with a VPN up that is the VPN's address (Facts,
106	    Settled, line 9).
107	  - While the port is on loopback, the dialog says the phone cannot reach
108	    it. Choosing an interface is a follow-up.
109	
110	## The record
111	
112	- **No new file, and no schema change.**
113	  - `devices.json` is unchanged. A browser is a `PairedDevice` whose
114	    `name` the page chose.
115	  - `identity.json` keeps its layout (`IDENTITY_SCHEMA_VERSION` is 1 at
116	    `src/ports/remote.rs:17`; store `SCHEMA_VERSION` is 16 at
117	    `src/core/model.rs:12`). Neither is bumped. Only the value of
118	    `certificate` changes when the certificate is reissued.
119	- **Reissue** (`src/adapters/remote.rs`):
120	  - `make_identity` issues through a new helper, `issue_certificate(key,
121	    server_id, names, now)`. `names` comes from `certificate_names()`:
122	    `127.0.0.1`, `localhost`, and `local_address()` when one exists. A
123	    fresh identity is therefore compliant from the start.
124	  - `certificate_facts(der) -> Option<CertFacts { not_after, ips }>`
125	    extends the DER walker that `spki_sha256_of_cert` (`:247`) already
126	    uses. It reads the validity and the iPAddress entries of the SAN
127	    extension. A certificate with no SAN yields no IPs.
128	  - `reissued(identity, key_pem, now) -> Option<Identity>` returns a new
129	    identity when any of these holds:
130	    - `certificate_facts` fails;
131	    - a name from `certificate_names()` is missing;
132	    - fewer than 30 days remain.
133	  - The key, `spki_sha256`, `server_id` and `created` are unchanged.
134	- **Where it runs.** In `SwitchboardApp::bind_remote` (`src/app.rs`,
135	  after the key is read and before `tls_config`):
136	  - The new identity is saved straight through
137	    `services.remote.save_identity`, as `make_identity` already does
138	    (`src/app.rs:2860`).
139	  - It is then handed to the core with `AppAction::CertificateReissued`,
140	    and TLS is built from it.
141	  - A failed save is logged, and the port listens with the old
142	    certificate. A reissue never blocks listening.
143	  - Startup binds through this same path, so no extra call is needed in
144	    `load_identity`.
145	- **Rehydration.** Nothing new on the host, because the page is in the
146	  binary. On the device, two things are stored:
147	  - The token, in an `HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict` cookie that no
148	    script can read.
149	  - Under `localStorage["switchboard:" + server_id]`, the public
150	    `{spki_sha256, device_id}`. These are not secrets. The page uses them
151	    only to tell "identity changed" apart from "not paired".
152	  - An address change is a new origin, so the device pairs again. The
153	    old record stays in the dialog until the owner revokes it.
154	
155	## The signals
156	
157	No new host signal. The page reacts to signals that already exist:
158	
159	| Signal | Page state |
160	|---|---|
161	| `/info` key differs from the URL's `key`, or `id` differs | "This address answers with a different key. Nothing was sent." |
162	| `/info` key differs from the stored key | "This Mac's identity changed. Pair again." |
163	| `GET device` 401, with a stored key that matches | "This device is no longer paired. Pair again from the Mac." |
164	| `GET device` 401, nothing stored | "Not paired" (below) |
165	| `/pair` 403 `pairing_closed` / `wrong_code` / `wrong_key` | The host's message, and "open pairing on the Mac and scan again" |
166	| socket `hello`, then `changed` / `removed` / `resync_required` | §4.4 reconcile, with polling off |
167	| socket close or error | `GET device`: a 401 is the revoked state; otherwise poll, and retry the socket after 5, 10, 30 and then 60 s |
168	| a 403 `scope` on `send` | Read `device` again and hide the box |
169	| `/info.version` differs from the version at load | `location.reload()` |
170	
171	The page reads `device` again on load, on every `hello`, and after any
172	403 `scope`. A scope raised in the dialog therefore shows at the next
173	reconnect or reload.
174	
175	## Actions and effects
176	
177	**Core**
178	- `AppAction::CertificateReissued(Identity)` replaces `identity` and
179	  leaves the devices, the pairing window and the rotation flag alone. It
180	  emits no effect, because the app saved the file before dispatching, as
181	  `IdentityLoaded` does. Routed in `src/core/action.rs:1248-1257` to
182	  `remote_action`.
183	- `pub fn pairing_url(identity: &Identity, code: &str, address:
184	  Option<SocketAddr>) -> Option<String>` in `src/core/remote.rs`. It is a
185	  pure format:
186	  - `https://<ip>:<port>/#code=<code>&key=<spki>&id=<server_id>`, with an
187	    IPv6 address in brackets;
188	  - `None` when there is no address.
189	
190	**Adapter** (`src/adapters/remote.rs`). These types are adapter types,
191	not contract.
192	- `RemoteRequest` (`:359-371`) gains four fields:
193	  - `host: Option<String>`, kept only if it matches
194	    `[A-Za-z0-9.:\[\]-]{1,255}`;
195	  - `origin: Option<String>`;
196	  - `page: bool`, true when the request carries `X-Switchboard-Page: 1`;
197	  - `cookies: Vec<(String, String)>`, only those whose name starts with
198	    `__Host-switchboard-`. Like `bearer`, these are never logged; `refuse`
199	    logs only the method and path (`src/app.rs:3754-3772`).
200	  - `read_request` (`:444-516`) fills these fields.
201	- `RemoteReply` (`:389-393`) gains `set_cookie: Option<String>`, a full
202	  header value. The 28 literals in `app.rs` gain `set_cookie: None`.
203	  `respond` (`:530-553`) writes the header when the field is set.
204	- `respond` also adds `Cache-Control: no-store` and
205	  `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` to every JSON reply.
206	- `session_cookie(server_id, token)` and `cleared_cookie(server_id)`
207	  build the header:
208	  - `__Host-switchboard-<server_id>=<token>; Path=/; Secure; HttpOnly;
209	    SameSite=Strict; Max-Age=34560000`;
210	  - the cleared form has `Max-Age=0`.
211	- **Paths outside `/api/v1/` never reach the frame.** In `connection`
212	  (`:770-876`), before the rate check and `try_send`, a request whose
213	  path does not start with `/api/v1/` is answered on the connection
214	  thread from `web::PAGE`, the way the 429 is:
215	  - `GET /`, `/app.js` or `/app.css` gets 200 with that file's headers;
216	  - any other method on those paths gets 405;
217	  - any other path gets 404 with the same `not_found` JSON body that
218	    `serve_remote` gives today, so
219	    `the_allowlist_refuses_everything_else_with_no_side_effect`
220	    (`tests/remote.rs:682`) keeps passing for `/api/v2/projects`.
221	  - Every one of these replies carries `Connection: close`, and the
222	    connection ends after it. The page's file loads therefore free their
223	    unauthenticated slot at once, and a burst of them cannot hold the
224	    four slots that `/pair` needs (Facts, Unresolved, line 39: build so
225	    that static files never starve `/pair`).
226	  - No rate window applies. These replies cost the frame nothing; the
227	    pool and the 5 s deadlines bound them.
228	  - The `strip_prefix` refusal in `serve_remote` (`src/app.rs:3023`)
229	    stays as a guard.
230	- **`src/adapters/web.rs`** (new) holds `PAGE: [(path, content_type,
231	  body); 3]`, built with `include_str!("../../web/…")`, and
232	  `headers(host: Option<&str>) -> Vec<(&str, String)>`:
233	  - `Content-Type`:
234	    - `text/html; charset=utf-8`;
235	    - `text/javascript; charset=utf-8`;
236	    - `text/css; charset=utf-8`.
237	  - `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; script-src 'self';
238	    style-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data:; connect-src 'self'
239	    wss://<host>; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'none'; frame-ancestors
240	    'none'`.
241	    - `wss://<host>` is listed explicitly because CSP's `'self'`
242	      covering `wss` is not in the facts file.
243	    - When `host` is missing, the directive is `connect-src 'self'`
244	      alone, and polling still works.
245	  - `Cache-Control: no-store`. Nothing is cached, so no version
246	    mismatch survives a reload.
247	  - `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`.
248	  - `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`.
249	  - `Connection: close`.
250	
251	**App** (`src/app.rs`)
252	- `authenticate` (`:3127-3157`) takes the token in this order:
253	  1. `bearer`, as today, for native clients;
254	  2. otherwise the cookie named `__Host-switchboard-<server_id>`, only
255	     when one of these holds:
256	     - `request.page` is set and this is not an upgrade;
257	     - this is an upgrade and `origin == "https://" + host`.
258	  - A cookie that fails either check is treated as no token.
259	  - A 401 to a request that presented this host's cookie carries
260	    `cleared_cookie`.
261	- `remote_pair` (`:3606-3674`) handles a body with `"cookie": true` this
262	  way: the reply leaves out `token` and sets `session_cookie`, so the
263	  page's script never sees the token. Without that field, the reply is
264	  as today.
265	- `("GET", ["device"])` comes right after `authenticate`, beside
266	  `events` (`:3036`). It answers `{device_id, name, scope}` in the
267	  envelope, with `authenticated: true`.
268	  - A cookie-authenticated reply sets `session_cookie` again, so a page
269	    in use never reaches the cookie's 400-day `Max-Age`.
270	- `remote_info` capabilities (`:3580`) gain `"device"` and `"page"`.
271	- `bind_remote`: the reissue above.
272	
273	**Native text path**
274	- `PairingInvite.parse` (`client/Sources/SwitchboardProtocol/Info.swift:114`)
275	  works like this:
276	  - Text that starts with `https://` is a URL. The host and port become
277	    the one address. The fragment's `code`, `key` and `id` become
278	    `code`, `spkiSha256` and `serverID`. A missing parameter is a parse
279	    error.
280	  - Any other text is decoded as JSON, as today.
281	  - `switchboard-remote pair` (`main.swift:111`), the headset's paste
282	    (`BrowserView.swift:883`) and `SWITCHBOARD_INVITE` (`:106`) all go
283	    through `parse`, so none of them changes.
284	- One QR, one text: the dialog no longer produces the JSON form.
285	  Accepting JSON in `parse` keeps old pasted invites and the fixture
286	  working.
287	
288	## Browser trust (decision 1)
289	
290	- **Choice: the click-through on the owner's own network is the trust
291	  step.**
292	  - It works in every browser.
293	  - A downloaded certificate works only on iOS, and only after a manual
294	    switch in Certificate Trust Settings (Facts, Settled, line 23).
295	    Whether Android trusts one is unresolved (Facts, Unresolved,
296	    line 37).
297	  - Offering a certificate download is a follow-up for the owner.
298	- **What the URL's `key` buys.** A genuine page sends the code only to a
299	  host whose `/info` key matches. That protects against an honest wrong
300	  host: a stale address, or a second instance on another port.
301	- **What it does not buy.** An impostor that wins the click-through
302	  serves its own script, and that script is not the genuine page.
303	  - The code never reached any server in the request line, because it
304	    sits in the fragment.
305	  - An impostor that relays `/pair` gets a reply with no token unless it
306	    terminates TLS itself, and the host refuses a key that is not its
307	    own (spec §5).
308	  - What is left is an active attacker on the LAN at the moment of the
309	    first scan. Accepting the warning is accepting that risk, and the
310	    dialog says so.
311	- **§5's rule, amended.** A non-loopback bind serves nothing before
312	  pairing except `/info`, `/pair`, and the three page files. The page
313	  files carry no state.
314	
315	## The UI
316	
317	**The Mac** (`src/ui/remote.rs`)
318	- The pairing window:
319	  - The QR and "Copy invite" (`:154-207`) carry `pairing_url(…)` instead
320	    of the JSON.
321	  - When there is no address, there is no QR, and the line reads "No
322	    network address; pair by typing the code".
323	  - When `!identity.listen.lan`, a line under the QR reads "A phone
324	    can't reach this Mac until Allow devices on the local network is
325	    on."
326	- Under the devices list, beside the redaction sentence (`:73-80`):
327	  "A browser can't check this Mac's key the way the headset does. The
328	  certificate warning you accept on a phone is the trust step. Accept it
329	  only on your own network, right after scanning."
330	- The devices list is otherwise unchanged. Browsers appear by the name
331	  they chose, with scope and Revoke as today.
332	
333	**The page** (`web/index.html`, `web/app.js`, `web/app.css`). Plain DOM,
334	no inline script or style, and `<link rel="icon" href="data:,">` so the
335	browser asks for no favicon.
336	- **Header:**
337	  - the host's `server_name`;
338	  - the device's scope as a "Read-only" or "Control" chip;
339	  - "Live" or "Live updates unavailable".
340	- **On load:**
341	  1. Take `location.hash`, then `history.replaceState(null, "", "/")`
342	     before anything else runs.
343	  2. `GET /api/v1/info`.
344	  3. Choose the state:
345	     - With an invite: compare `key` and `id` with what `/info` presents,
346	       show "Pair as [name] · Pair", and post `/pair {code, device_name,
347	       spki_sha256: key, cookie: true}`. Store the public record and go
348	       on.
349	     - Without an invite: compare the stored key with `/info`'s, then
350	       `GET device`.
351	  4. Open the socket, and poll until it says `hello`.
352	- **Unpaired with no invite:** "Not paired. On the Mac, open Remote
353	  devices, choose Allow pairing, then scan the code with this device."
354	- **List:**
355	  - The page reads `projects`, `projects/{id}/sessions` for each
356	    project, and `waiting`.
357	  - Waiting sessions come first in a group of their own, each with a dot
358	    and its reason.
359	  - Below them, the sessions are grouped by project. Each row shows the
360	    name, the kind, the `card` word and liveness, and an excerpt where
361	    one was read.
362	- **Session view:**
363	  - A Claude Code session shows `last-response` (Codex has no parser;
364	    design.md "Known gaps"). Any other session shows `screen?lines=60`.
365	  - Over the socket, the page sends `watch {conversation|screen, id}` and
366	    fetches after `watching`, refetching on `changed`. With no socket,
367	    it reads every 5 s.
368	- **Reply box:**
369	  - Shown only when `scope == "control"`.
370	  - Posts `sessions/{id}/send {op: crypto.randomUUID(), text}`.
371	    `randomUUID` is available because the page is a secure context
372	    (Facts, Settled, line 12).
373	  - On a timeout, the page reads `ops/{op}` and follows §4.5's rule. It
374	    never resends blindly.
375	- Every `fetch` sends `X-Switchboard-Page: 1` and
376	  `credentials: "same-origin"`. All API paths live in one `API` object
377	  at the top of `app.js`, which is what the test reads.
378	
379	## The tests
380	
381	**Core** (`src/core/tests.rs`)
382	- `CertificateReissued` replaces the identity, keeps the devices, the
383	  open window and `identity_rotated`, and emits nothing.
384	- `pairing_url`:
385	  - IPv4 gives the exact string;
386	  - IPv6 is bracketed;
387	  - no address gives `None`.
388	
389	**Adapter units** (`src/adapters/remote.rs`)
390	- `make_identity`'s certificate:
391	  - `certificate_facts` reads `127.0.0.1` in its SAN and a `not_after`
392	    no more than 825 days out;
393	  - its SPKI still equals `spki_sha256`.
394	- `reissued`:
395	  - an old-style certificate (no SAN), a near expiry, or a missing
396	    address each yield a new certificate with the same SPKI;
397	  - a current certificate yields `None`.
398	- `read_request` keeps `host`, `origin`, `X-Switchboard-Page` and only
399	  the `__Host-switchboard-` cookies, and drops a malformed `Host`.
400	
401	**Integration** (`tests/remote.rs`)
402	- The `http` helper (`:245-296`) returns the response headers and takes
403	  extra request headers.
404	- `the_page_is_served_with_its_headers_and_references_only_served_paths`:
405	  - `/`, `/app.js` and `/app.css`, unpaired, on a listener, each get 200
406	    with:
407	    - the `Content-Type` above;
408	    - the CSP, with `wss://localhost` for `Host: localhost`;
409	    - `Cache-Control: no-store`, `nosniff` and `Connection: close`.
410	  - Every `src=` and `href=` in `index.html` (except `data:`) is one of
411	    the served paths.
412	  - Every `/api/v1/…` template in `app.js`'s `API` object, with seeded
413	    ids filled in, answers a paired request with something other than
414	    `404 not_found`.
415	- `a_path_outside_the_api_is_answered_without_the_frame`:
416	  - `/favicon.ico` gets 404 `not_found` with `Connection: close`;
417	  - `POST /` gets 405;
418	  - `port.poll` stayed empty.
419	- `a_browser_pairs_by_cookie_and_reads_and_subscribes_with_it`:
420	  - `/pair` with `cookie: true` has no `token` in the body, and its
421	    `Set-Cookie` matches the attributes above.
422	  - `GET device` with the cookie and the page header gets 200 and the
423	    scope; with the cookie and no page header, 401.
424	  - An upgrade with the cookie and `Origin: https://localhost` gets
425	    `hello`; with another origin, 401.
426	  - After a revoke, `GET device` gets 401 with a cleared cookie.
427	  - A bearer request still works.
428	- `device_reports_the_scope_as_the_dialog_sets_it`: `GET device` follows
429	  `SetDeviceScope`.
430	- `a_page_load_burst_leaves_room_for_pair`: four static GETs in flight at

432	
433	**UI** (`tests/ui.rs`)
434	- With the pairing window open and `listen.lan` false, the
435	  "can't reach" line is shown.
436	- The trust sentence is present.
437	- "Copy invite" copies text that starts with `https://`.

439	**Swift** (`swift test` in `client/`)
440	- `testInviteParsesTheQRText` stays.
441	- A new `testInviteParsesTheURL` covers an IPv4 URL and a URL missing

447	**Live acceptance.** The owner runs it, on a scratch data directory.
448	- Setup: `SWITCHBOARD_SCRIPT` with `remote-listen lan 0` and `pairing
449	  <code>`, plus `SWITCHBOARD_DATA_DIR` and `SWITCHBOARD_TMUX_SOCKET`.

463	**Docs, in the same commit**
464	- `docs/remote-client.md`:
465	  - §4.1: paths outside the API answered on the connection thread, with

467	  - §4.3: rows for `/`, `/app.js`, `/app.css` and `GET /api/v1/device`.

# A web page on the remote port (issue #230)

The host serves a small page from the remote port it already has. Any
browser on the local network opens it, pairs from a URL in the pairing
window's QR code, lists the sessions with the waiting ones first, shows
a session's last response or screen, and sends a reply. The API is the
one the headset uses, plus one small read. The page is three files
under `web/`, embedded with `include_str!`. There is no build step and
no dependency.

Line numbers are as of 7fe8949 in this worktree. "Facts" means
`facts/1/repo/facts.md`, cited by section and line.

## Where this departs from the issue

- **The pairing data goes in the fragment, not the query.** The URL is
  `https://<ip>:<port>/#code=…&key=…&id=…`.
  - A fragment never appears in the request line or in `Referer` (Facts,
    Settled, line 17). The code therefore never reaches the host's
    `RemoteRequest.query`, a proxy, or a log. A `?code=` would reach all
    three before any page script runs.
  - The page still calls `history.replaceState` first. Whether Safari,
    iCloud or the camera keep the original URL is unresolved (Facts,
    Unresolved, line 35), so the plan does not depend on it. The code's
    protection is what it already is: single use, five minutes, and
    three failures close the window.
- **Pairing waits for one tap, with a name field.**
  - The page shows "Pair as [name]" with a default taken from the user
    agent, and posts `/pair` only when the owner taps Pair.
  - The tap is needed because iPadOS Safari may identify itself as a Mac
    (Facts, Unresolved, line 36), and the dialog has no way to rename a
    device. So the name has to be chosen on the page.
- **The events socket is an enhancement. Polling is the default.**
  - Whether `wss://` connects in Safari after a certificate click-through
    is unresolved (Facts, Unresolved, lines 28–33).
  - The page first works by polling: `waiting` every 5 s, the open
    session's read every 5 s, and the lists every 30 s, only while the
    tab is visible.
  - When the socket opens, the page follows §4.4 and stops polling. When
    the socket fails, the header says "Live updates unavailable".
  - Under either answer, "a waiting session moves to the top without a
    reload" holds.
- **The page needs one new read: `GET /api/v1/device`.** It answers
  `{device_id, name, scope}`.
  - Only the `/pair` reply tells a device its scope (Facts, Settled,
    line 7), and the reply box depends on scope.
  - The page's first authenticated call on load is this read, so a 200
    or 401 here also decides between "paired" and "pair again".
- **Not every session gets a one-line excerpt.**
  - `SessionView` has no excerpt field (`control/src/lib.rs:637`). The
    Mac builds its excerpt from the transcript in
    `src/ui/cards.rs:558`, and the headset reads `last-response` once
    per session (`client/Sources/SwitchboardUI/BrowserView.swift:152-155`).
  - The cost of that on real data is unresolved (Facts, Unresolved,
    line 40). So the page reads `last-response` only for waiting Claude
    Code sessions, at most 8 of them, and for the session that is open.
  - Every other row shows its `waiting_reason`, or its `card` word.
  - An excerpt field on `SessionView` is a follow-up.
- **The certificate is reissued over the same key.** The issue does not
  mention this.
  - Today's certificate has no SAN, no EKU, and a `not_after` in the year
    4096 (`src/adapters/remote.rs:95-110`; Facts, Settled, line 10).
    Apple says connections with such a certificate "will fail" (Facts,
    Settled, line 11). Whether Safari or Chrome still offer a
    click-through for it is unresolved (Facts, Unresolved, line 27).
  - The plan builds a compliant certificate:
    - a SAN for the LAN IP, `127.0.0.1` and `localhost`;
    - the serverAuth EKU;
    - a validity of 800 days, reissued when fewer than 30 days remain or
      when the current address is missing from the SAN.
  - The SPKI does not change, so every native pin stays valid (spec §5:
    "a certificate reissued from the same key … still verifies").
- **A browser's acceptance of the certificate is not permanent.**
  - Chrome forgets a bypass after 7 days (Facts, Settled, line 18), so on
    Chrome the warning comes back once a week.
  - How long Safari remembers one is unresolved (Facts, Unresolved,
    line 34). The page assumes nothing about it.
- **"Identity changed" appears after the browser's own warning.**
  - After a key rotation, the browser shows its interstitial before any
    page script runs (Facts, Settled, lines 18–19).
  - Once the owner accepts, the page compares `/info`'s key with the one
    it stored at pairing and shows "identity changed, pair again".
- **The page learns "revoked" over REST, never from the socket.**
  - A refused upgrade reaches the page only as a 1006 close (Facts,
    Settled, line 15). The page therefore follows every socket close
    with a `GET device` call. A 401 there shows "No longer paired".
  - The host gives a revoked device and a rotated pairing the same 401
    (`src/app.rs:3127-3157`). The page tells them apart from the key it
    stored, not from the reply.
- **`SameSite=Strict` does not isolate one port from another.**
  - Every port on one IP is same-site, and a cookie is sent to all of
    them (Facts, Settled, line 16).
  - To keep two instances from colliding, the cookie is named after the
    `server_id`.
  - To stop another page on the same IP from riding on the cookie, a
    cookie is accepted only on a request carrying `X-Switchboard-Page: 1`
    (a cross-origin page cannot send that header without a preflight the
    host never answers), or on an upgrade whose `Origin` is the host's
    own (Facts, Settled, line 13: browsers must send `Origin`).
  - The plan accepts that the cookie also reaches any other HTTPS service
    on the owner's own Mac's IP. That cost buys a token that no script
    can read.
- **The QR's address has to be reachable.**
  - The QR prints `local_address()` even while the port is bound to
    loopback, and with a VPN up that is the VPN's address (Facts,
    Settled, line 9).
  - While the port is on loopback, the dialog says the phone cannot reach
    it. Choosing an interface is a follow-up.

## The record

- **No new file, and no schema change.**
  - `devices.json` is unchanged. A browser is a `PairedDevice` whose
    `name` the page chose.
  - `identity.json` keeps its layout (`IDENTITY_SCHEMA_VERSION` is 1 at
    `src/ports/remote.rs:17`; store `SCHEMA_VERSION` is 16 at
    `src/core/model.rs:12`). Neither is bumped. Only the value of
    `certificate` changes when the certificate is reissued.
- **Reissue** (`src/adapters/remote.rs`):
  - `make_identity` issues through a new helper, `issue_certificate(key,
    server_id, names, now)`. `names` comes from `certificate_names()`:
    `127.0.0.1`, `localhost`, and `local_address()` when one exists. A
    fresh identity is therefore compliant from the start.
  - `certificate_facts(der) -> Option<CertFacts { not_after, ips }>`
    extends the DER walker that `spki_sha256_of_cert` (`:247`) already
    uses. It reads the validity and the iPAddress entries of the SAN
    extension. A certificate with no SAN yields no IPs.
  - `reissued(identity, key_pem, now) -> Option<Identity>` returns a new
    identity when any of these holds:
    - `certificate_facts` fails;
    - a name from `certificate_names()` is missing;
    - fewer than 30 days remain.
  - The key, `spki_sha256`, `server_id` and `created` are unchanged.
- **Where it runs.** In `SwitchboardApp::bind_remote` (`src/app.rs`,
  after the key is read and before `tls_config`):
  - The new identity is saved straight through
    `services.remote.save_identity`, as `make_identity` already does
    (`src/app.rs:2860`).
  - It is then handed to the core with `AppAction::CertificateReissued`,
    and TLS is built from it.
  - A failed save is logged, and the port listens with the old
    certificate. A reissue never blocks listening.
  - Startup binds through this same path, so no extra call is needed in
    `load_identity`.
- **Rehydration.** Nothing new on the host, because the page is in the
  binary. On the device, two things are stored:
  - The token, in an `HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict` cookie that no
    script can read.
  - Under `localStorage["switchboard:" + server_id]`, the public
    `{spki_sha256, device_id}`. These are not secrets. The page uses them
    only to tell "identity changed" apart from "not paired".
  - An address change is a new origin, so the device pairs again. The
    old record stays in the dialog until the owner revokes it.

## The signals

No new host signal. The page reacts to signals that already exist:

| Signal | Page state |
|---|---|
| `/info` key differs from the URL's `key`, or `id` differs | "This address answers with a different key. Nothing was sent." |
| `/info` key differs from the stored key | "This Mac's identity changed. Pair again." |
| `GET device` 401, with a stored key that matches | "This device is no longer paired. Pair again from the Mac." |
| `GET device` 401, nothing stored | "Not paired" (below) |
| `/pair` 403 `pairing_closed` / `wrong_code` / `wrong_key` | The host's message, and "open pairing on the Mac and scan again" |
| socket `hello`, then `changed` / `removed` / `resync_required` | §4.4 reconcile, with polling off |
| socket close or error | `GET device`: a 401 is the revoked state; otherwise poll, and retry the socket after 5, 10, 30 and then 60 s |
| a 403 `scope` on `send` | Read `device` again and hide the box |
| `/info.version` differs from the version at load | `location.reload()` |

The page reads `device` again on load, on every `hello`, and after any
403 `scope`. A scope raised in the dialog therefore shows at the next
reconnect or reload.

## Browser trust (decision 1)

- **Choice: the click-through on the owner's own network is the trust
  step.**
  - It works in every browser.
  - A downloaded certificate works only on iOS, and only after a manual
    switch in Certificate Trust Settings (Facts, Settled, line 23).
    Whether Android trusts one is unresolved (Facts, Unresolved,
    line 37).
  - Offering a certificate download is a follow-up for the owner.
- **What the URL's `key` buys.** A genuine page sends the code only to a
  host whose `/info` key matches. That protects against an honest wrong
  host: a stale address, or a second instance on another port.
- **What it does not buy.** An impostor that wins the click-through
  serves its own script, and that script is not the genuine page.
  - The code never reached any server in the request line, because it
    sits in the fragment.
  - An impostor that relays `/pair` gets a reply with no token unless it
    terminates TLS itself, and the host refuses a key that is not its
    own (spec §5).
  - What is left is an active attacker on the LAN at the moment of the
    first scan. Accepting the warning is accepting that risk, and the
    dialog says so.
- **§5's rule, amended.** A non-loopback bind serves nothing before
  pairing except `/info`, `/pair`, and the three page files. The page
  files carry no state.

## The UI

**The Mac** (`src/ui/remote.rs`)
- The pairing window:
  - The QR and "Copy invite" (`:154-207`) carry `pairing_url(…)` instead
    of the JSON.
  - When there is no address, there is no QR, and the line reads "No
    network address; pair by typing the code".
  - When `!identity.listen.lan`, a line under the QR reads "A phone
    can't reach this Mac until Allow devices on the local network is
    on."
- Under the devices list, beside the redaction sentence (`:73-80`):
  "A browser can't check this Mac's key the way the headset does. The
  certificate warning you accept on a phone is the trust step. Accept it
  only on your own network, right after scanning."
- The devices list is otherwise unchanged. Browsers appear by the name
  they chose, with scope and Revoke as today.

**The page** (`web/index.html`, `web/app.js`, `web/app.css`). Plain DOM,
no inline script or style, and `<link rel="icon" href="data:,">` so the
browser asks for no favicon.
- **Header:**
  - the host's `server_name`;
  - the device's scope as a "Read-only" or "Control" chip;
  - "Live" or "Live updates unavailable".
- **On load:**
  1. Take `location.hash`, then `history.replaceState(null, "", "/")`
     before anything else runs.
  2. `GET /api/v1/info`.
  3. Choose the state:
     - With an invite: compare `key` and `id` with what `/info` presents,
       show "Pair as [name] · Pair", and post `/pair {code, device_name,
       spki_sha256: key, cookie: true}`. Store the public record and go
       on.
     - Without an invite: compare the stored key with `/info`'s, then
       `GET device`.
  4. Open the socket, and poll until it says `hello`.
- **Unpaired with no invite:** "Not paired. On the Mac, open Remote
  devices, choose Allow pairing, then scan the code with this device."
- **List:**
  - The page reads `projects`, `projects/{id}/sessions` for each
    project, and `waiting`.
  - Waiting sessions come first in a group of their own, each with a dot
    and its reason.
  - Below them, the sessions are grouped by project. Each row shows the
    name, the kind, the `card` word and liveness, and an excerpt where
    one was read.
- **Session view:**
  - A Claude Code session shows `last-response` (Codex has no parser;
    design.md "Known gaps"). Any other session shows `screen?lines=60`.
  - Over the socket, the page sends `watch {conversation|screen, id}` and
    fetches after `watching`, refetching on `changed`. With no socket,
    it reads every 5 s.
- **Reply box:**
  - Shown only when `scope == "control"`.
  - Posts `sessions/{id}/send {op: crypto.randomUUID(), text}`.
    `randomUUID` is available because the page is a secure context
    (Facts, Settled, line 12).
  - On a timeout, the page reads `ops/{op}` and follows §4.5's rule. It
    never resends blindly.
- Every `fetch` sends `X-Switchboard-Page: 1` and
  `credentials: "same-origin"`. All API paths live in one `API` object
  at the top of `app.js`, which is what the test reads.

I've made both changes in the review copy of the plan, `review/1/repo/plan.md`, and re-read the file to check each one is there. The earlier plan under `plan/1/repo/` is unchanged. My answers are in `review/1/repo/plan.response-1.md`.

1. **The certificate check runs only at bind.**
   - The plan now has one method, `refresh_certificate`. It runs at bind, right after pairing opens (before the QR is drawn), on every poll while the pairing window is open, and once an hour otherwise. The hourly check also covers renewing before the 30-day mark in an app that runs for a long time.
   - The QR now prints the address the certificate was last checked against, not a fresh `local_address()`, so it can't show an IP that isn't in the certificate.
   - I didn't take the rebind the feedback suggested. A rebind would make every already-paired connection's next request fail with a 503, and would drop the event sockets. Instead the port swaps the certificate in place through a rustls cert resolver, so new connections get the new certificate and open ones carry on.
   - A new integration test moves the address and opens pairing. It checks that the new certificate carries the new address with the same key, and that an open paired connection still works.

2. **Nothing settles that a browser keeps the cookie after a certificate warning.**
   - The cookie stays where the token lives. A new section, "The implementer's first test: does the cookie hold", makes this the first step of the work.
   - The implementer builds the cookie path on the host with a throwaway probe page that never gets committed. You then run it on the iPhone and any other browser you mean to support: pair, then the `GET device` read has to return 200, including after a reload.
   - If that fails, the implementer stops and reports. The fallback is a token held by the page's own script, sent as a header and on the WebSocket. It isn't built in this commit; it's now listed under the follow-ups for you.

content.content:
- The SPKI does not change, so every native pin stays valid (spec §5:
    "a certificate reissued from the same key … still verifies").
- **A browser's acceptance of the certificate is not permanent.**
  - Chrome forgets a bypass after 7 days (Facts, Settled, line 18), so on
    Chrome the warning comes back once a week.
  - How long Safari remembers one is unresolved (Facts, Unresolved,
    line 34). The page assumes nothing about it.
- **"Identity changed" appears after the browser's own warning.**
  - After a key rotation, the browser shows its interstitial before any
    page script runs (Facts, Settled, lines 18–19).
  - Once the owner accepts, the page compares `/info`'s key with the one
    it stored at pairing and shows "identity changed, pair again".
- **The page learns "revoked" over REST, never from the socket.**
  - A refused upgrade reaches the page only as a 1006 close (Facts,
    Settled, line 15). The page therefore follows every socket close
    with a `GET device` call. A 401 there shows "No longer paired".
  - The host gives a revoked device and a rotated pairing the same 401
    (`src/app.rs:3127-3157`). The page tells them apart from the key it
    stored, not from the reply.
- **`SameSite=Strict` does not isolate one port from another.**
  - A failed save is logged, and the port keeps serving the old
    certificate. A reissue never blocks listening.
  - It is called from four places:
    - `bind_remote`, after the key is read and before `tls_config`, so
      startup and a listen change serve a current certificate;
    - right after the app dispatches `AppAction::OpenPairing`, which runs
      before the next frame draws the QR;
    - on each once-a-second poll while `pairing_at(now)` is open, so an
      address that moves while the window is up reissues before a scan;
    - on `Tick` at most once an hour otherwise, so a long-running app
      renews before the 30-day mark and follows a moved address.
  - The poll-time call is cheap when nothing moved: one UDP
    `connect` for the address and a comparison against the SAN IPs that
    `certificate_facts` read when the certificate was last set, cached on
    the app.
- **Rehydration.** Nothing new on the host, because the page is in the
  binary. On the device, two things are stored:
  - The token, in an `HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict` cookie that no
  page's script never sees the token. Without that field, the reply is
  as today.
- `("GET", ["device"])` comes right after `authenticate`, beside
  `events` (`:3036`). It answers `{device_id, name, scope}` in the
  envelope, with `authenticated: true`.
  - A cookie-authenticated reply sets `session_cookie` again, so a page
    in use never reaches the cookie's 400-day `Max-Age`.
- `remote_info` capabilities (`:3580`) gain `"device"` and `"page"`.
- `refresh_certificate` and its four callers, above.
- `DrawCtx` (`src/ui/mod.rs:401`) gains `remote_address: Option<IpAddr>`,
  filled from `certified_address` beside `remote_port` (`:420`).

**Native text path**
- `PairingInvite.parse` (`client/Sources/SwitchboardProtocol/Info.swift:114`)
  works like this:
  - Text that starts with `https://` is a URL. The host and port become
    the one address. The fragment's `code`, `key` and `id` become
    `code`, `spkiSha256` and `serverID`. A missing parameter is a parse
    error.
  - Any other text is decoded as JSON, as today.
  - `switchboard-remote pair` (`main.swift:111`), the headset's paste
    (`BrowserView.swift:883`) and `SWITCHBOARD_INVITE` (`:106`) all go
    through `parse`, so none of them changes.
- One QR, one text: the dialog no longer produces the JSON form.
  Accepting JSON in `parse` keeps old pasted invites and the fixture
  - A bearer request still works.
- `opening_pairing_after_the_address_moved_serves_a_certificate_for_it`:
  - bind with the address override at `10.0.0.1`; an unpinned handshake
    reads that IP in the SAN;
  - with a paired bearer connection kept open, set the override to
    `10.0.0.2` and dispatch `OpenPairing`;
  - a new handshake reads `10.0.0.2` in the SAN with the same SPKI, the
    kept connection still answers 200, and `certified_address` is
    `10.0.0.2`;
  - with the window open, moving the override to `10.0.0.3` and running
    one poll does the same.
- `device_reports_the_scope_as_the_dialog_sets_it`: `GET device` follows
  `SetDeviceScope`.
- `a_page_load_burst_leaves_room_for_pair`: four static GETs in flight at
  once, then `/info` and `/pair`, all succeed.

- With the pairing window open and `listen.lan` false, the
  "can't reach" line is shown.
- The trust sentence is present.
- "Copy invite" copies text that starts with `https://`.

- `testInviteParsesTheQRText` stays.
